newsitem.title: CANADA: Hundreds trapped on Canadian ice floe.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds trapped on Canadian ice floe.

text.p: At least 500 ice fishermen and snowmobilers were trapped on a lake about 45 miles (70 km) north of Toronto on Saturday, stranded by shifting ice.
The Canadian Forces and three police forces sent in helicopters, boats and emergency crews to rescue them.
There were no injuries immediately reported.

A seven-mile (11-km)-long crack about 30 yards (metres) wide stranded the people, along with their fishing huts and vehicles, on Lake Simcoe, police said. The crack broke on Saturday afternoon during a fishing derby, isolating at least 500 people at one end of the lake.
"Every rescue service around is involved," said one officer.
While at least 68 people had been rescued by early evening, others had to endure hours of waiting in strong winds and freezing temperatures.
"It's all due to the recent weather," said Ontario Provincial Police Sergeant Denis Michaud in nearby Orillia. "With the high winds and the currents and pressures, you get shifting ice."
